description: The head of commercial legal must approve a conditional assignment package for a software license being transferred with a divested business, including the transfer condition and the buyer's access during the operational handoff, with input from IP counsel and carve-out counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company is transferring its analytics division to a buyer next month, and the division relies on a third-party software platform.
shared_context.S2: The current assignment draft transfers the company's software rights to the buyer at closing.
shared_context.S3: The software vendor has been informed of the transaction but has not yet signed the assignment document.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly carve-out review, Elena asks IP counsel and carve-out counsel for concise reports of required conditions and operational protections, then makes the approval decision at the end of that review.

PF1.text: While reviewing the original license from the vendor's legacy contract archive, Marcus found an anti-assignment clause requiring the vendor's prior written consent and stating that the consent must name the buyer as the permitted successor; the circulated contract abstract omitted this clause, so Marcus has not yet added it to the approval materials.

PF2.text: Nina confirmed with the division's operations lead yesterday that the buyer needs uninterrupted access to the platform for exactly 120 days after closing while its replacement system is configured; that operational requirement has not yet been added to the transition schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The assignment package must be approved subject to the required conditions.
The vendor's prior written consent must be required.
The consent must name the buyer as the permitted successor.
The assignment must become effective only after that written consent is obtained.
The buyer must receive exactly 120 days of uninterrupted platform access.
The package must include a commitment to preserve the 120-day uninterrupted access period.

decisive_facts.why: The omitted anti-assignment clause changes approval from an ordinary transfer at closing to a conditional approval requiring vendor consent that names the buyer and makes the assignment effective only after consent.
The operations confirmation changes the transition terms from unspecified access to exactly 120 days of uninterrupted platform access and requires a matching transition commitment.
